result.verdict: I found no change in the five commits that breaks a live scheduled job tomorrow. All checks were read-only. (1) keystone.ps1 Invoke-MeetingSync: I tested this on pwsh 7.5.2 with ErrorActionPreference=Stop, the setting it inherits from morning-cadence.ps1. `$x = @(& native 2>&1)` sets $LASTEXITCODE to the native exit code (3 in the test). Invoking the $reportFailure scriptblock leaves it alone. Redirected stderr does not throw. A failed `security` lookup gives LASTEXITCODE 1 and an empty $key, which leaves the old behaviour in place. The Keychain read should not hang or prompt today. The login keychain is set to `no-timeout`, so it does not lock after inactivity or sleep. The item exists with acct=kristinarash, and `security -w` reads it without a prompt. The session's own test ran as a gui-domain LaunchAgent (com.keystone.kctest, bootstrapped and kickstarted) and logged user=kristinarash and 37 bytes, which also shows $env:USER is set under launchd. The call has no timeout of its own. If a prompt ever appeared, run-job.ps1 would kill the cadence after 30 minutes; on weekdays reconcile then retries up to 3 times a day and gives up. So the worst case is bounded. Output stays on Write-Host and the return value is unchanged, so no caller that parses output is affected. The fireflies-intake skill updated .sync-state.json at 23:19 tonight, so tomorrow's export step has almost nothing to catch up on. Before 09-26 the same export path worked on the Mac ("New exports: 2"). (2) daily-backup.ps1 step 2b-harvest: $U, $DryRun, $Errors and $IsMacOS are all in scope at script level. Log() calls no native command, so $LASTEXITCODE after `(& /bin/bash … 2>&1 | Out-String)` is still bash's exit code (tested: 2). A dry-run copy of the harvest loop, using both Homebrew rsync and /usr/bin/openrsync under a bare launchd-style environment, covered 116 repos with 0 failures in about 1 s. The _DRIVE symlink is only stat'ed, which launchd allows, and is then skipped. Nothing in the harvest makes the backup end ERROR every day. (3) jobs.json: the file parses. I ran the restored pattern through run-ledger's Test-Probe: True for 10-23, matching `[2026-10-23T06:01:04.1726120-05:00] cadence OK`. The old pattern returned False because it threw a "range in reverse order" error that was caught. Test-JobCompleteOn checks the ledger first, so the probe can only turn "no success" into "succeeded". It cannot add a make-up run. Tomorrow is Saturday, and the schedule kind is weekdays, so reconcile skips the job (Test-ScheduledOn is False on 10-24). `keystone-reconcile.ps1 -DryRun` reports all jobs current. Not from these commits: the morning plist has no Weekday key, so it fires 7 days a week while jobs.json says weekdays. (4) register.ts: the mod's fs.read rejects files over 4 MiB, and daily-backup.ps1 trims its log once it passes 2 MB (now 771 KB). The regex takes 0 ms on the real log and returns OK. If the read ever fails, the catch falls back to null and the line just says no status. The mod loads from ~/.claude/mods/job-watch (.loadlist entry 2), and there is no second copy. (5) The six ops/ plists and scripts/com.keystone.nightlydigest.plist match the installed LaunchAgents exactly. verify-backup.ps1's new exit 1 has no scheduled or skill caller. No live code, plist, settings hook or mod refers to any deleted .ps1 or .md. The remaining mentions are comments, Windows-only branches, or .bak files. refresh_all_data.bat had no live steps. The skills SKILL.md change is text only. In TOS_Evidence_Brief, parents[2] resolves to ~/DEV, and both Baylor_Doc_Style/baylor_docstyle.py and Tech_Inventory_Analysis/scripts/doc_platform.py exist. Not reported as defects: recallStatus's \w+ also captures the words baseline/no from check.py's other messages. The new sync_error message blames the key for every sync_error, but cadence.log shows one past transient GraphQL error. The two real issues are both minor and both in nightly-digest.py.

defects.defect: The new crash handler cannot report a failure while loading claude-files-digest.py (fd). The import (lines 38-40) and `MAX_BODY = fd.MAX_BODY` (line 54) run when the module loads, before the try at line 309. If they fail, the handler never runs. The handler itself also needs fd.ERR_LOG. So the commit's claim that "a crash now reaches .errors.log" covers only crashes inside main().
defects.evidence: Line 38: `_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("files_digest", SCRIPTS / "claude-files-digest.py")`. Line 40: `_spec.loader.exec_module(fd)`. Line 54: `MAX_BODY = fd.MAX_BODY`. All three are top-level statements. The handler is `if __name__ == "__main__": try: sys.exit(main()) except Exception as e: ... with fd.ERR_LOG.open("a") ...`. A syntax error or renamed constant in claude-files-digest.py would show only in logs/nightlydigest.err, with nothing in .errors.log.
defects.fix: Define ERR_LOG in nightly-digest.py (HOME/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log). Move the fd import and MAX_BODY into a function called inside the try, or wrap lines 38-40 in their own try/except that writes to that ERR_LOG and exits 1.

defects.defect: The newly scheduled 21:00 job makes one send attempt with no retry. Notes in the repo say the Mac is usually asleep at 21:00, so launchd will often run the job right after wake, before the network is up. The gws send then fails, the email is lost, and a FAILED line lands in .errors.log. Nothing tries again.
defects.evidence: daily-backup-login.sh lines 7-8: "every 21:00 run from 10-13 to 10-22 ended ERROR because the Mac slept on battery". claude-files-digest.log uses the same fd.GWS gmail +send path and failed at wake: `[2026-10-23T06:36:08] FAILED 2026-10-22: error[discovery]: ... dns error: failed to lookup address information`. A later attempt at 06:54 succeeded. nightly-digest.py main() calls subprocess.run([*fd.GWS, "gmail", "+send", ...]) once, and on a non-zero exit it logs FAILED, writes .errors.log and returns 1.
defects.fix: Before sending, wait for network: resolve www.googleapis.com, or retry the send about 3 times at 60 s intervals, and treat only the last failure as an error. Alternatively, add a successProbe-based make-up path such as a reconcile entry, or schedule the job at a time the Mac is reliably awake.
